title: Runtime telemetry entropy reduction and dashboard hygiene (notes and plan)
content:
Purpose:
This note is a pragmatic plan to reduce telemetry 'entropy' across runtime inference services and bring dashboards back to signal-first, not noise-first. The goal is to reduce alert fatigue, lower query cost, and improve investigation turn-around by: consolidating metrics, tightening measurement contracts, anchoring traces to clear session keys, and pruning dashboards into a small set of investigative surfaces.

Context and motivation:
- Over the last 9 months we added many metrics for experiments, A/B, and perf hunts. Result: high cardinality, duplicated gauges, and panels that rarely help incident resolution.
- Cost: big queries on historical token latency percentiles and span reassembly are expensive and slow.
- Ops pain: oncall spends too long triaging noisy alerts caused by metric duplication and improper cardinality.

High level objectives (3 months):
1) Define measurement contracts for top 12 runtime signals (who owns, units, retention, cardinality caps).
2) Implement a trace anchoring pattern and sampling budget that lets us reconstruct session-level failures without full-fidelity retention.
3) Reduce dashboard panel count in the 'runtime' space by 60% — keep only investigation-first widgets.
4) Run a short pilot (2 teams) that enforces contracts and tracks triage time reduction.

Scope and exclusions:
- Scope: serving runtime, KV-cache layer, router, batching, and model-host orchestration.
- Exclude: user-facing product metrics (GTM analytics), billing metrics owned by finance.

Measurement contracts (proposal):
- Contract fields: metric_name, type (gauge/counter/histogram), unit, canonical_tags (allowed list), cardinality_limit, owner, retention_policy.
- Example: "inference.token_generation_latency_ms"
  - type: histogram
  - unit: ms
  - canonical_tags: [region, model_variant, route] (no endpoint_id, no session_token)
  - cardinality_limit: 3 tags = 1000 unique time-series per cluster
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime
  - retention: 90d coarse, 7d fine
- Example: "kv_cache.hit_rate" (gauge)
  - tags: [model_variant] only
  - measured as a 1m rolling value

Metric naming and dedup rules:
- Enforce prefix policy: inference.* for request-level; runtime.* for host-level; infra.* for node metrics.
- If a metric already exists with the same semantic meaning, owners must file a deprecation jira before adding new ones.

Trace anchoring strategy:
- Problem: full sampling at scale is costly and unnecessary. We need reconstructability not full-fidelity replay.
- Anchor definition: a trace anchor = {session_id, request_id, primary_route, sample_tag} attached to a small set of spans emitted at: router ingress, batcher start, model host start, and error boundary.
- Sampling policy (budgeted):
  - 2% full-trace retention globally for production traffic (adaptive: increase to 5% for prod incidents window).
  - 10% sparse retention where only anchor spans + context headers are retained (for long-term trending).
  - Always retain traces for 100% of requests marked as errors >= 5xx or user-facing latency > p99_slo_threshold.
- Instrumentation notes: make anchors idempotent, ensure session_id is propagated through batcher and model host and logged to logs.

Dashboard hygiene playbook:
- Audit each runtime dashboard panel against 3 axis: signal usefulness (high/med/low), cost-to-render (query cost), and owner clarity.
- Keep panels that map directly to triage steps (e.g., token_p50/p95 latency by route, queue_depth, kv_cache_hit_rate). Remove panels that are derivative and rarely used.
- Consolidation recipe: replace many per-tenant panels with a single multi-select panel with drop-down to limit to top-5 tenants by traffic.
- Recommended dashboards to keep:
  - Investigation landing (compact): single row SLO, token latency p50/p95, error rate, top-3 slowdown routes.
  - Runtime health (host-level): CPU/GPU util, mem pressure, OOM counts, queue latency.
  - Cost guard: query volume, model-invocations per-minute, token compute-ms.

Quantization & aggregation guidance:
- Use histograms for latency with consistent bucket boundaries across services. Avoid custom buckets per team.
- Aggregation windows: 1m for operational dashboards, 1h for cost/capacity ones.

Investigation flow (mapping telemetry to runbook):
1) Start at the compact investigation landing dashboard. If SLO breached -> check route-level token p95 and queue depth.
2) If queue depth high, open batcher dashboard and check batch_size_distribution and inflight requests.
3) If batcher normal but model latency high, use trace-anchor sampler to reconstruct representative traces for the route in the incident window.
4) Use KV cache metrics to check for cache thrash (hit_rate drop correlated with latency spike).

Quick wins (first 2 weeks):
- Remove 12 duplicate metrics flagged in metric-inventory sheet (see linked JIRA).
- Add canonical tag enforcement in the ingestion pipeline for inference.* metrics (deploy shim to sanitize tags).
- Implement anchor spans on router and model-host (PR ready in obs repo).

Pilot plan (8 weeks):
- Week 0: baseline triage time and alert noise (metrics: mean time to ack, false positive alert rate).
- Week 1–2: apply measurement contracts for Team A (batcher + model-host) and Team B (router + router-autoscaler).
- Week 3–6: monitor, iterate, remove low-value panels, tune sampling.
- Week 7–8: compare triage time and alert volume vs baseline; decide org-wide rollout if >25% improvement.

Open questions and risks:
- How strict should cardinality caps be for customer-specific tags? (tradeoff: investigatability vs cost).
- Will existing SDKs support renaming / deprecating metrics without breaking dashboards? Need migration tooling.
- Risk: policing tags could break some repos that rely on ad-hoc labels.

Action items (owners):
- Claire: prepare measurement-contract template and sample jira for metric deprecation (due 2025-11-10).
- Marco: build ingestion tag sanitizer shim and smoke test (due 2025-11-18).
- Priya: PR for anchor spans instrumentation and sampling hooks (draft by 2025-11-12).
- Ethan: inventory dashboard panels and mark keep/remove/merge (deliverable: 2025-11-14).

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Consider adding a lightweight 'investigate' API that returns the top-k anchor traces for a given route and time window (could be a lambda on top of trace store).
- Long-term: explore an index of unusual cardinalities (auto-detect new tags) so teams are notified before metric explosion.

References and shortcuts:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/metric-contracts-draft (see section 3 for template)
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1423 (metric inventory), JIRA-OBS-204 (trace anchors)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/264 (anchor spans)

Status: draft — soliciting feedback from eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, and SRE.

-- end --
